problem: Prior semantic-map VLN methods (VLMaps) cannot separate multiple instances of the same object. The authors' own SI Maps are 2D top-down and closed-set (Mask2Former), so larger objects hide smaller ones and the LLM must map queries onto known class labels.
motivation: Real-world language queries refer to specific instances and to objects outside any fixed label set. Foundation models (RAM, Grounding DINO, SAM, CLIP, DINOv2) make an open-set, instance-level 3D map possible without training.
key_idea: Build an open-set 3D point-cloud map with instance-level CLIP and DINOv2 embeddings by merging per-frame Grounded-SAM masks across views, then localise the LLM-parsed target by CLIP text-embedding similarity.
insight: Combining semantic similarity (DINOv2 cosine) with 3D volumetric overlap lets the map keep separate instances apart (nearby chairs) while merging repeated views of one object. Moving from a closed-set 2D map to an open-set 3D map raised Success Rate over SI Maps (0.82 vs 0.72 human evaluation). There is no ablation of individual components, so the gain is only attributed to the open-set and 3D nature.
method: Open-set instance detection: RAM tags each RGB image, unwanted tags (wall, floor, ceiling) are filtered, Grounding DINO produces boxes for the tags, and SAM produces class-agnostic masks (Grounded-SAM).
Semantic embeddings: the crop of each object is encoded with CLIP and DINOv2 and L2-normalised, so each instance carries both embeddings.

3D back-projection: masks and depth are lifted to point clouds using camera intrinsics and pose (GT pose in simulation, RTAB-Map with G2O in the real world). Background is removed, then voxel downsampling and DBSCAN keep the largest cluster, and an oriented 3D bounding box is computed.

Incremental fusion: new detections are merged into existing nodes when an aggregate of DINOv2 cosine similarity and nearest-neighbour volumetric overlap exceeds a threshold, otherwise they become new nodes. Merged embeddings are averaged with weights by source count.
Scene refinement: an overlap matrix merges duplicate nodes caused by occlusion or viewpoint change, and nodes with too few points or detections are discarded.

Language grounding: ChatGPT 3.5 maps commands to function primitives (object description plus instance index). The description's CLIP embedding is ranked against the map's instance embeddings by cosine similarity to pick the instance.

Goal generation: a top-down occupancy grid is built from the point cloud and obstacles are inflated by the robot radius. BFS finds reachable free cells, and the free cell closest to the target centroid is sent to the ROS Navigation Stack.

setting.backbone: Frozen foundation models: RAM, Grounding DINO, SAM, CLIP, DINOv2, plus ChatGPT 3.5 for command parsing
setting.training_data: none (training-free, composed of pretrained foundation models)
setting.observation: posed RGB-D image sequence (Kinect Azure on the robot, iPad in some sequences); pose from GT in simulation or RTAB-Map in the real world
setting.action_space: goal point in a 2D occupancy grid executed by the ROS Navigation Stack (high-level goal; no low-level learned actions)
setting.simulator: Habitat with Matterport3D scenes (mapping data), plus real-world scenes
setting.privileged: Ground-truth camera poses in simulation; the map is built offline from a pre-recorded RGB-D traversal of each scene before queries are run

numbers_note: The only quantitative table (Table 1) reports Success Rate on a custom evaluation (5 Matterport3D scenes with 5,267 frames plus real-world scenes) that is not one of the canonical benchmarks, so it is not entered as a numbers row. Values as printed: O3D-SIM 0.82 human / 0.84 automatic; SI Maps K=9 0.72 / 0.74; SI Maps K=5 0.70 / 0.74; VLMaps with CC 0.48 / 0.52; VLMaps 0.40 / 0.46. The caption says '5 different scenes from Matterport3D and 1 real world environment', while the text mentions six real-world scenes.
results: On a custom set of open-set and closed-set language queries, O3D-SIM reaches Success Rate 0.82 (human) and 0.84 (automatic). The strongest baseline, SI Maps (K=9), gets 0.72 and 0.74, and VLMaps with CC gets 0.48 and 0.52. Qualitatively, the map finds objects outside closed-set vocabularies (mannequin, wheelchair, mobile robot) and identifies 5 of 6 tables.
limitations: Evaluation is small and non-standard (custom queries, a few scenes, Success Rate only, no VLN benchmark), and there are no ablations of the components.
The map is offline and static, so dynamic objects and humans are not handled. It also requires accurate poses and heavy foundation models, and LLM query parsing takes 45-60 s per command.
